subject.name: NodeRoom note-shaped surfaces, after the note-surface fix — color and elevation on NoteworthyInbox and NotebookDigestWorkbench
subject.surface: The same color carriers as the baseline receipt (score-noderoom-note-surfaces-single-accent-inline-before), re-scored after the feat/note-surface-dna change. NodeRoom's terracotta stays the app's own hue; nothing here adopts Mew's teal.
subject.evidenceRef: source, noderoom branch feat/note-surface-dna: work-artifacts.css (span[data-type] now var(--accent-ink), block index chip achromatic), src/app/styles.css (.r-inbox-why-text b now var(--accent-ink); popover shadow unchanged at 0 12px 32px)

appliesWhenSatisfied: text-dominant surfaces where inline metadata must be scannable: unchanged from the baseline receipt
dark-first product with a single named accent: unchanged

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: data visualization surfaces needing categorical palettes (dataviz skill governs there)
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Unchanged: neither surface renders a chart.

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.clause: status-heavy dashboards where semantic red/amber/green carry meaning the accent cannot
doesNotApplyWhenChecked.note: Unchanged: semantic state colors on trust surfaces (failed, suggested, accepted/ready, needs_review) were exempted per element in the baseline and were not touched by the fix — rule-single-accent-inline may not override trust-surface neutrality, and did not.

anchors.0: two or more non-semantic hues loose in body text and the accent spent on per-entry decoration — color cannot function as a retrieval signal
anchors.1: one foreign non-semantic hue remains inline, or the accent decorates every entry uniformly
anchors.2: no foreign inline hue and no per-entry accent decoration, but no meaningful inline accent carrier exists either — color encodes nothing retrievable
anchors.3: the accent is carried by meaningful inline elements; chrome accent or elevation still sits past the measured bound (shadows over 8px blur or above 0.067 alpha, obs-mew-tokens/f5)
anchors.4: one accent hue carried only by meaningful inline elements, achromatic chrome, every shadow within the measured tokens (obs-mew-tokens/f1, f5)

criteria.question: Does any non-semantic hue outside the app accent appear on inline elements?

citations.note: The periwinkle #b8c7ff on typed-block labels is gone; the labels now carry var(--accent-ink) — the app's one accent, in the app's own hue. No other non-semantic foreign hue was found inline on either surface.
Colored inline elements on these surfaces are now accent-or-semantic only, which is the condition under which color can work as a retrieval signal.

criteria.finding: No foreign inline hue remains. Green on accepted/ready stays as semantic state, exempt as in the baseline.

criteria.question: Is the accent spent on uniform per-entry decoration rather than on meaning?

citations.note: The block index chip lost its accent tint and ink and is now muted mono text with no background. The accent no longer appears on all entries uniformly; it appears where something is typed, pending, or named.

criteria.finding: Accent decoration on every entry is gone; a terracotta element on these surfaces now means something is there.

criteria.question: Does any meaningful inline element carry the accent, making color a retrieval signal?

citations.note: Two inline carriers now exist: typed-block labels in the digest meta row, and entity names in the inbox why-panel (.r-inbox-why-text b). Chrome accent remains on affordances — the batch-research button and practice panel border — which keeps this at the rung below inline-only.

criteria.finding: Meaningful inline accent carriers exist on both surfaces. The residual chrome accent on affordances was not among the baseline's lowest criteria and was left alone.

criteria.question: Do shadows stay within the measured bound — at most 8px blur at 0.05-0.067 alpha?

citations.note: Unchanged from baseline: the inbox popover keeps box-shadow 0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.18). It scored 2 at baseline — not the lowest criterion — so under this task's fix-the-lowest method it was deliberately not touched, and it stays 2 rather than being quietly rescored.

criteria.finding: Unimproved and recorded as such. Whether an overlay container is bound by an entry-surface elevation rule is a fair dispute for humanReview; this receipt keeps the instrument's number.

scoreBasis: Ladder: the subject sits at the highest anchor it fully satisfies. c1 and c2 clear the foreign-hue and decoration rungs; c3 places accent on meaningful inline elements; c4's overlay shadow keeps anchor 4 closed.
notScored: Semantic state colors on trust surfaces — unchanged and untouched by design, as in the baseline receipt.
Whether the chrome grays are hue-linked to the terracotta accent (obs-mew-tokens/f3) — still requires a computed-style audit; still not assessed.
Contrast ratios of var(--accent-ink) on the tinted needs_review background — an accessibility question this rule does not govern; the token pair already ships elsewhere in this stylesheet.
Runtime computed styles — not audited, same limit as the baseline.
boundary: Scored from source on branch feat/note-surface-dna, diffed against commit 9c99889f. The absence-of-foreign-hue claim rests on grep over both stylesheets for hex literals in the touched component blocks; a hue introduced by JavaScript at runtime would evade it, and none was found in the two components' TSX.
scoredBy: note-surface corpus scoring pass, noderoom feat/note-surface-dna, against note-surface.single-accent-inline.rule.json unmodified
